skill.name: azure-resource-manager-durabletask-dotnet
skill.description: Use Azure Resource Manager SDK examples to manage Durable Task Scheduler resources in .NET. It covers scheduler provisioning, task hubs, retention policies, authentication, listing, updates, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Guide .NET agents through Azure Durable Task Scheduler management with Azure Resource Manager.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static findings were adjudicated as false positives because they are Markdown code fences, inline identifiers, official reference links, private example CIDRs, or placeholder Azure credential variables. No prompt injection, hidden command execution, or credential exfiltration evidence was found in SKILL.md. A semantic finding remains for destructive Azure deletion examples that should require clear confirmation before use.

remediation.issue: Examples include DeleteAsync calls that remove task hubs and schedulers.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning before deletion examples and recommend confirmation of subscription, resource group, and scheduler names.

remediation.issue: The environment variable section names AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed identity or workload identity guidance, and mark service principal secrets as optional local setup only.

remediation.issue: Sample IP allowlists use private placeholder ranges.
remediation.suggestion: State that readers must replace sample CIDR ranges with approved ingress ranges before deployment.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Durable Task Resources in .NET
content.value_statement: Provisioning Durable Task Scheduler resources with ARM SDKs can be confused with data-plane orchestration work. This skill provides focused .NET guidance for schedulers, task hubs, retention policies, authentication, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use the management-plane Durable Task SDK instead of data-plane orchestration packages.
Shows package installation and Azure Identity setup for .NET ARM clients.
Demonstrates creating Dedicated and Consumption Durable Task Schedulers.
Covers task hub creation, scheduler listing, lookup, update, and deletion flows.
Includes retention policy management and ARM error handling patterns.
Lists related SDK packages and official source references.
limitations: Provides guidance only; it does not run Azure commands or verify cloud state.
Does not cover data-plane orchestration, activities, events, or instance queries.
Examples use placeholder resource names, subscriptions, regions, and private IP ranges.
Users must verify Azure permissions, quotas, API versions, and deletion impact.

use_cases.title: Plan scheduler provisioning
use_cases.description: Create a management-plane plan for Durable Task Scheduler, SKU choice, task hub setup, and retention policy handling.

use_cases.title: Add ARM management to tooling
use_cases.description: Use .NET ARM SDK patterns to add scheduler create, update, list, and delete workflows to deployment tools.

use_cases.title: Select the correct Durable Task SDK
use_cases.description: Compare management-plane resource operations with data-plane orchestration packages before choosing dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a scheduler
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the .NET ARM SDK steps to create a Durable Task Scheduler with Azure Identity and a task hub.

prompt_templates.title: Configure retention
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a Durable Task retention policy to an existing scheduler and explain the required resource hierarchy.

prompt_templates.title: Review update flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned scheduler update for SKU capacity and IP allowlist changes before I implement it.

prompt_templates.title: Design production provisioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production-safe Durable Task Scheduler provisioning workflow with RBAC, idempotent updates, error handling, and deletion safeguards.

output_examples.input: Need a new Durable Task Scheduler with a task hub.
output_examples.output: A response separates package setup, Azure Identity authentication, scheduler creation, task hub creation, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Need to update a scheduler allowlist.
output_examples.output: A response identifies the existing scheduler, replaces placeholder CIDR ranges, uses the documented update flow, and recommends change review.

output_examples.input: Need to understand which Durable Task package to use.
output_examples.output: A response explains that Azure.ResourceManager.DurableTask manages Azure resources, while client and worker packages run orchestrations.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with least-privilege Azure RBAC for management operations.
Replace all placeholder resource names, regions, and IP allowlists before implementation.
Require explicit confirmation before applying updates or deleting Azure resources.
anti_patterns: Using this management SDK to start orchestrations or query running instances.
Copying sample CIDR ranges or resource names into production deployments.
Running cleanup or delete examples against shared subscriptions without review.

faq.question: Is this skill for running orchestrations?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure Resource Manager operations for schedulers, task hubs, and retention policies.

faq.question: Does the skill execute Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation guidance. Generated code can call Azure only when a user runs it.

faq.question: Which packages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.ResourceManager.DurableTask, Azure.Identity, Azure.ResourceManager, and related Durable Task client and worker packages.

faq.question: Does it store credentials?
faq.answer: No. It shows placeholder environment variable names and recommends DefaultAzureCredential for authentication.

faq.question: Can it help with deletion workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows deletion order, but users should confirm subscription, resource group, scheduler, and task hub names first.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in the marketplace report.
